title: Why Does a Cold Can Sweat?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why does a cold can sweat?
The water isn't leaking out. The can is sealed.
Warm air is full of invisible water vapour.
On a hot, humid day, one cubic metre of air carries about twenty-five grams of it.
The air touching a can from the fridge chills to nearly fridge temperature.
That cold, no more than about six grams per cubic metre can stay as vapour.
The rest has nowhere to go, so it turns back into liquid, right on the can.
It's the same as morning dew, or the fog on your glasses when you step out of an air-conditioned room.
The can isn't sweating. The air is.
